Trolls des Neiges

Les Trolls des Neiges sont des prédateurs solitaires du Grand Nord. Ils parcourent les étendues enneigées à la recherche de nourriture et possèdent une ténacité exceptionnelle : lorsqu’ils choisissent une proie, ils peuvent la suivre pendant des jours ou des semaines. Leur Culture est entièrement adaptée à la neige, à la glace, aux longues nuits septentrionales et à l’hibernation estivale.

Mode de vie

Leur zone de chasse peut être immense. Ils connaissent plusieurs grottes, crevasses, cavités sous la glace ou ruines plutôt qu’une unique tanière. Les longues nuits de l’hiver sont leur période la plus favorable, tandis que l’été et ses longues heures de lumière entraînent une hibernation dans un refuge profond.

La poursuite est le trait culturel le plus remarquable. Un Troll des Neiges peut reprendre une piste après un repos, suivre une direction générale et continuer longtemps après qu’une proie pense l’avoir semé. Le Pistage sur neige, la Survie arctique et l’endurance de déplacement sont donc centraux.

Ils chassent animaux du Nord, phoques et poissons, et préfèrent volontiers la chair des autres peuples lorsqu’ils peuvent en obtenir. Leurs armes sont simples : griffes, armes récupérées, pierres et surtout morceaux de glace lancés. Le labba constitue leur langue étrangère la plus caractéristique.

Refuge et lumière solaire

La tanière ou le refuge doit protéger efficacement de la lumière solaire. Cette vulnérabilité appartient à la Race, mais elle organise toute la vie culturelle : activité nocturne, connaissance des abris, attention au lever du jour et préférence pour les grottes, ruines, ravins ou autres lieux couverts. Un Troll expérimenté connaît plusieurs refuges possibles sur son territoire.

Nourriture et chasse

La nourriture constitue une motivation fondamentale. La viande domine, complétée selon l’environnement par gibier, ressources trouvées et prises de raids. La chasse développe Pistage, patience, connaissance du terrain et parfois collets. Les membres d’autres peuples peuvent devenir des proies lorsque l’occasion se présente.

Société et famille

La société reste très simple. Autorité, propriété et conflits sont réglés de manière concrète, souvent par la force. Les structures politiques complexes, administrations et institutions savantes sont absentes. Les formes de famille et de groupement varient selon la population troll, mais l’apprentissage reste presque entièrement pratique.

Tempérament

Les Trolls sont généralement lents, brutaux, peu sophistiqués et quelque peu paresseux. Ils peuvent néanmoins apprendre des habitudes efficaces lorsque celles-ci répondent directement à la nourriture, au territoire, au combat ou à une contrainte imposée par un maître. Leur intelligence limitée n’empêche pas l’expérience pratique.

Langues

La capacité linguistique est faible chez la plupart des Tereg primitifs. La communication repose beaucoup sur bruits, gestes et actions. Les individus les plus intelligents peuvent apprendre labba dégradé et éventuellement orcien. La lecture et l’écriture restent marginales et les concepts concrets sont nettement plus faciles à exprimer que les idées abstraites.

Vêtements et artisanat

Les vêtements sont rares et grossiers, principalement faits de peaux et de cuir. Le Travail du cuir et le Travail de la pierre restent utilitaires : sangle, manteau, arme simple, agrandissement d’un refuge ou déplacement de blocs. La finesse artisanale et la décoration ne sont pas des priorités.

Armes et armures

Les armes favorisent la masse et la simplicité : gourdins, masses, marteaux, pierres ou projectiles improvisés selon la population. Les griffes et autres armes naturelles appartiennent à la Race mais leur usage peut être développé par la Culture. Les armures lourdes sont rares chez les Trolls primitifs et proviennent généralement d’un maître extérieur lorsqu’elles existent.

Magie et religion

Les Tereg primitifs ne possèdent normalement ni religion structurée ni tradition magique autonome. Ils peuvent servir une puissance de l’Ombre par peur ou contrainte. Les objets enchantés qu’ils possèdent ont presque toujours été trouvés ou volés et peuvent rester incompris.

Relations

Les Khazâd constituent des ennemis particulièrement détestés dans de nombreuses traditions troll. Les relations avec Orcs et Humains dépendent du contexte : proies, rivaux, alliés forcés ou maîtres. Une puissance extérieure suffisamment forte peut employer un Troll comme garde, soldat ou force de choc.

Compétences culturelles

Le profil favorise très fortement Pistage, Survie arctique ou toundra, Armes de jet, Combat naturel, Spéléologie, Développement corporel, Approche furtive et Dissimulation. Escalade, Fabrication de pièges, Cueillette, Travail du cuir et connaissance de la faune soutiennent la vie septentrionale.

Race et Culture

La Race Troll porte stature, force, peau naturelle, griffes, sens, résistances et réaction au Soleil. La Culture porte environnement, chasse, armes apprises, langues, comportement social, artisanat rudimentaire et compétences de terrain. Les mêmes avantages physiologiques ne doivent jamais être comptés deux fois.

Disponibilité et création

Cette Culture est disponible aux Premier, Deuxième, Troisième et Quatrième Âges. Un personnage joueur représente généralement un individu exceptionnel, capable de communiquer suffisamment avec un groupe. Sa tanière, son ancien maître éventuel, sa relation aux autres Trolls et une motivation concrète — nourriture, territoire, vengeance, perte d’un refuge ou butin — définissent immédiatement son histoire.

Langues de départ

Snow Trolls

Snow Trolls are solitary predators of the Far North. They roam snowy expanses in search of food and possess exceptional tenacity: once they choose a quarry, they can follow it for days or weeks. Their Culture is wholly adapted to snow, ice, the long northern nights, and summer hibernation.

Way of life

Their hunting range can be enormous. They know several caves, crevasses, hollows beneath the ice, or ruins rather than a single lair. The long nights of winter are their most favorable season, while summer and its long hours of daylight bring on hibernation in a deep refuge.

Pursuit is their most remarkable cultural trait. A Snow Troll can take up a trail again after resting, follow a general direction, and continue long after its prey believes it has escaped. Tracking over snow, Arctic Survival, and endurance in travel are therefore central.

They hunt northern animals, seals, and fish, and readily prefer the flesh of other peoples when they can obtain it. Their weapons are simple: claws, scavenged weapons, stones, and especially thrown chunks of ice. Labba is their most characteristic foreign language.

Shelter and sunlight

The lair or refuge must provide effective protection from sunlight. This vulnerability belongs to the Race, but it shapes the whole Culture: nocturnal activity, knowledge of shelters, attention to sunrise, and a preference for caves, ruins, ravines, or other covered places. An experienced Troll knows several possible refuges within its territory.

Food and hunting

Food is a fundamental motivation. Meat predominates, supplemented according to the environment by game, scavenged resources, and the spoils of raids. Hunting develops Tracking, patience, knowledge of the terrain, and sometimes trapping. Members of other peoples can become prey when the opportunity arises.

Society and family

Society remains very simple. Authority, property, and disputes are settled in concrete ways, often by force. Complex political structures, administrations, and scholarly institutions are absent. Forms of family and grouping vary among Troll populations, but learning remains almost entirely practical.

Temperament

Trolls are generally slow, brutal, unsophisticated, and somewhat lazy. They can nevertheless learn effective habits when those habits directly concern food, territory, combat, or a constraint imposed by a master. Limited intelligence does not prevent practical experience.

Languages

Linguistic ability is poor among most primitive Tereg. Communication relies heavily on noises, gestures, and actions. The more intelligent individuals can learn broken Labba and possibly Orcish. Reading and writing remain marginal, and concrete concepts are far easier to express than abstract ideas.

Clothing and craft

Clothing is rare and crude, made mainly from hides and leather. Leatherworking and Stoneworking remain utilitarian: straps, cloaks, simple weapons, enlarging a refuge, or moving blocks of stone. Fine craftsmanship and decoration are not priorities.

Weapons and armor

Weapons favor mass and simplicity: clubs, maces, hammers, stones, or improvised missiles depending on the population. Claws and other natural weapons belong to the Race, but their use can be developed through Culture. Heavy armor is rare among primitive Trolls and, when it exists, usually comes from an outside master.

Magic and religion

Primitive Tereg normally possess neither an organized religion nor an independent magical tradition. They may serve a power of the Shadow through fear or coercion. Enchanted objects in their possession have almost always been found or stolen and may remain poorly understood.

Relations

Khazâd are particularly hated enemies in many Troll traditions. Relations with Orcs and Humans depend on circumstance: prey, rivals, forced allies, or masters. A sufficiently powerful outside force can employ a Troll as a guard, soldier, or shock troop.

Cultural skills

The profile very strongly favors Tracking, Arctic or Tundra Survival, Thrown Weapons, Natural Combat, Caving, Body Development, Stalking, and Hiding. Climbing, Trapmaking, Foraging, Leatherworking, and knowledge of wildlife support northern life.

Race and Culture

The Troll Race carries stature, strength, natural hide, claws, senses, resistances, and reaction to the Sun. Culture carries environment, hunting, learned weapons, languages, social behavior, rudimentary craft, and terrain skills. The same physiological benefits must never be counted twice.

Availability and character creation

This Culture is available in the First, Second, Third, and Fourth Ages. A player character generally represents an exceptional individual capable of communicating well enough with a group. Its lair, any former master, its relationship with other Trolls, and a concrete motivation — food, territory, revenge, the loss of a refuge, or loot — immediately define its story.

Starting Languages

They hunt northern animals, seals, and fish, and readily prefer the flesh of other peoples when they can obtain it. Their weapons are simple: claws, scavenged weapons, stones, and especially thrown chunks of ice. Labba is their most characteristic foreign language.

Shelter and sunlight

The lair or refuge must provide effective protection from sunlight. This vulnerability belongs to the Race, but it shapes the whole Culture: nocturnal activity, knowledge of shelters, attention to sunrise, and a preference for caves, ruins, ravines, or other covered places. An experienced Troll knows several possible refuges within its territory.

Food and hunting

Food is a fundamental motivation. Meat predominates, supplemented according to the environment by game, scavenged resources, and the spoils of raids. Hunting develops Tracking, patience, knowledge of the terrain, and sometimes trapping. Members of other peoples can become prey when the opportunity arises.

Society and family

Society remains very simple. Authority, property, and disputes are settled in concrete ways, often by force. Complex political structures, administrations, and scholarly institutions are absent. Forms of family and grouping vary among Troll populations, but learning remains almost entirely practical.

Temperament

Trolls are generally slow, brutal, unsophisticated, and somewhat lazy. They can nevertheless learn effective habits when those habits directly concern food, territory, combat, or a constraint imposed by a master. Limited intelligence does not prevent practical experience.

Languages

Linguistic ability is poor among most primitive Tereg. Communication relies heavily on noises, gestures, and actions. The more intelligent individuals can learn broken Labba and possibly Orcish. Reading and writing remain marginal, and concrete concepts are far easier to express than abstract ideas.

Clothing and craft

Clothing is rare and crude, made mainly from hides and leather. Leatherworking and Stoneworking remain utilitarian: straps, cloaks, simple weapons, enlarging a refuge, or moving blocks of stone. Fine craftsmanship and decoration are not priorities.

Weapons and armor

Weapons favor mass and simplicity: clubs, maces, hammers, stones, or improvised missiles depending on the population. Claws and other natural weapons belong to the Race, but their use can be developed through Culture. Heavy armor is rare among primitive Trolls and, when it exists, usually comes from an outside master.

Magic and religion

Primitive Tereg normally possess neither an organized religion nor an independent magical tradition. They may serve a power of the Shadow through fear or coercion. Enchanted objects in their possession have almost always been found or stolen and may remain poorly understood.

Relations

Khazâd are particularly hated enemies in many Troll traditions. Relations with Orcs and Humans depend on circumstance: prey, rivals, forced allies, or masters. A sufficiently powerful outside force can employ a Troll as a guard, soldier, or shock troop.

Cultural skills

The profile very strongly favors Tracking, Arctic or Tundra Survival, Thrown Weapons, Natural Combat, Caving, Body Development, Stalking, and Hiding. Climbing, Trapmaking, Foraging, Leatherworking, and knowledge of wildlife support northern life.

Race and Culture

The Troll Race carries stature, strength, natural hide, claws, senses, resistances, and reaction to the Sun. Culture carries environment, hunting, learned weapons, languages, social behavior, rudimentary craft, and terrain skills. The same physiological benefits must never be counted twice.

Availability and character creation

This Culture is available in the First, Second, Third, and Fourth Ages. A player character generally represents an exceptional individual capable of communicating well enough with a group. Its lair, any former master, its relationship with other Trolls, and a concrete motivation — food, territory, revenge, the loss of a refuge, or loot — immediately define its story.
